Piper Sandler initiated coverage of the artificial intelligence (AI) chip and semiconductor sector, assigning "Overweight" ratings to AMD, Arm, Broadcom, Marvell Technology, and NVIDIA, while assigning "Neutral" ratings to Intel and Qualcomm. Zhitong Finance APP reports that Piper Sandler has published a research note initiating coverage of the artificial intelligence (AI) chip and semiconductor sectors. The firm launched ratings on seven major semiconductor stocks, assigning "Overweight" ratings to AMD (AMD.US), Arm (ARM.US), Broadcom (AVGO.US), Marvell Technology (MRVL.US), and NVIDIA (NVDA.US), while Intel (INTC.US) and Qualcomm (QCOM.US) received "Neutral" ratings. The firm identified Broadcom and NVIDIA as its "top picks" in the AI accelerator space, while highlighting AMD and Arm for their gains in server CPU market share. Regarding price targets, Piper Sandler assigned $600 to AMD, $320 to Arm, $460 to Broadcom, $110 to Intel, $270 to Marvell Technology, $300 to NVIDIA, and $190 to Qualcomm. Analysts David O'Connor and Zackary Altman stated in the report that computing power is the core foundation of AI development. With the explosive adoption of agentic AI, the industry urgently requires additional computing capacity. The firm noted that production capacity for 2027 is already sold out, and the order book for 2028 is fully booked. Piper Sandler projects that the computing power market will reach $2.2 trillion by 2030, comprising a $2 trillion accelerator market and a $200 billion CPU market. This implies a fivefold expansion of the computing power market by 2030, driving revenue growth across the supply chain and translating into an approximate 45% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) in earnings per share for this group of stocks. The firm believes these companies are the most critical participants in infrastructure build-outs by hyperscale cloud providers and emerging cloud vendors. The report also highlights that current scarcity in computing power is evident in the GPU-hour pricing of new cloud providers. According to Silicon Data's H100 pricing index, the hourly rate for NVIDIA's H100 GPU is $2.60, up from $2.00 in December prior to the emergence of OpenClaw. The report also mentioned a surge in demand in February 2025 driven by increased requirements from DeepSeek deployments. Declining computing costs further stimulate usage, which in turn continues to drive up demand for computing power. Piper Sandler emphasized that NVIDIA began mass-producing the H100 in the fourth quarter of 2022, meaning the chip is nearly four years old in terms of technological iteration. Additionally, component costs are rising, boosting hardware manufacturers' revenues; the firm found that GPU chip costs have increased from 30% to 40% over the last two product generations. On an individual stock level, O'Connor described NVIDIA as the "absolute leader in AI computing power," holding an 80% market share. He stated that the explosion of agentic AI workloads this year has led to a step-change in demand, with supply likely remaining tight for the next two to three years. He characterized the stock as "one of the lowest-valued stocks in the AI sector," trading at approximately 14 times its expected fiscal 2028 valuation. O'Connor identified Broadcom as the leader in custom ASIC chips with a 75% market share, noting issues with supply constraints. He wrote, "Demand is twice the supply, so securing additional capacity is key." He also pointed out that the company's visible market demand for fiscal year 2027 has reached 12 gigawatts. O'Connor described AMD as the "best beneficiary of agentic AI," noting its continued market share gains in server CPUs and the ramp-up of its Helios GPU, with anchor customers including OpenAI, Meta (META.US), and Anthropic. He projected that AMD's earnings would grow at a 65% compound annual growth rate by 2030. The analysts also expressed optimism about Marvell Technology's data center business, describing its $120 billion agreement with Google (GOOGL.US) as transformative. They also mentioned that the analyst day on October 6 could serve as a potential catalyst. Finally, O'Connor emphasized Arm's dominant position in the CPU intellectual property sector and its expansion into custom chips and accelerator IP, which he believes could double Arm's profitability.
